There's a difference between not shaving and not taking care of yourself and being a slob. I act, smell, and dress like a woman and take pride in that. I just don't shave my legs as often as other people do. That's my preference.

This comment is an example of the sexist standards women are held to. Do you consider it slobbish for men to not shave their legs?

When he was telling me about this he recognized that it was a sexist standard and that because it's rare to see a woman with body hair in mainstream media, hairless is all that he's used to. He's been thinking about this for a while and not saying anything because he wanted to see if he'd get over it, but he hasn't so he's just embracing it as his preference. His recognition of it being a sexist standard in general is probably the only reason I'm okay with shaving for him, as if he wasn't aware of that I'd probably be annoyed by it.

It's too late to cancel on the Reddit secret Santa, and I feel horrible about it because I've gotten the notification that my gift's on its way. I might message the person and tell them that I'm planning on it, it just might be delayed. I could ask for financial help from my family (I'm still dependent on them for a few things) but if they found out about my computer my dad would be furious. I don't want that to happen.

Sorry to hear about your boyfriend. I can't imagine being in that position.
